pageCache.pageTitle: Hever C of E Primary School - Home
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Welcome to Hever Church of England Primary School, a small village school, nestled in beautiful surroundings in Hever village.
At Hever CEP School, we offer a welcoming and inclusive learning environment where wellbeing and high standards of academic achievement go hand in hand. We value and celebrate diversity and are committed to enabling every child to build the confidence and resilience to flourish. Each child is supported to develop academically, socially, morally and spiritually, to create happy and well-rounded individuals. We are committed to ensuring that our children receive the best possible start to their education and leave us ready to take their role as confident and responsible young people, ready for the challenges and successes of their secondary education and our diverse society beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: Hever C of E Primary School - Afterschool Care

Afterschool Care
Afterschool care is provided by the school and is available from 3.15pm to 6pm Mondays to Thursdays and until 5.15pm on a Friday and last day of term. Please book via ParentMail.
Parents can book via ParentMail and pay instantly or chose to pay via the Government's Tax-free Childcare scheme. All children receive a snack when they arrive at afterschool club and there is an option to have food provided by Emma's Kitchen. Food is served at 4.45 pm. Please see the attached menu for further details.

3.15-5.15pm - £12 (without food)

4.15-6pm - £15 (no food)

pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Hever Church of England Primary School, a one-form entry village school, nestled in beautiful surroundings in Hever village.
At Hever CEP School, we offer a welcoming and inclusive learning environment where wellbeing and high standards of academic achievement go hand in hand. We value and celebrate diversity and are committed to enabling every child to build the confidence and resilience to flourish. Each child is supported to develop academically, socially, morally and spiritually, to create happy and well-rounded individuals. We are committed to ensuring that our children receive the best possible start to their education and leave us ready to take their role as confident and responsible young people, ready for the challenges and successes of their secondary education and our diverse society beyond.
Our Christian vision, centred on the story of Jesus Walks on the Water (Matthew 14: 22-33), sets high expectations for our whole school community to challenge and support each other to:
At Hever CEP School, we provide an ambitious and vibrant curriculum that builds a strong foundation and fosters a love of learning, within a safe and stimulating environment. Forest School, which is part of the curriculum for all children, provides opportunities to develop self-confidence and build strategies to assess and take risks safely. Every child’s contribution is valued and from the very beginning, we encourage independence and resilience so children have the confidence to recognise mistakes as an integral part of learning.
Our school benefits from strong partnerships with parents and carers, governors and the wider locality including Hever Castle and Bore Place. We work closely with Rev. Simon Braid from St. Peter’s Church and our Christian values underpin all aspects of our provision. These collaborations extend and enhance the core curriculum, providing real life and memorable opportunites beyond the classroom, enriching the children’s experiences and wider learning.
If our website is your first experience of Hever CEP School, then please allow us to extend a warm invitation to make a personal visit to see first-hand the stimulating education and diverse opportunities our children experience at Hever School. Please contact the school office who will be happy to arrange this.
Mrs Helene Bligh Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Hever C of E Primary School - Prospective Parents
pageCache.text:
Prospective Parents
Welcome to Hever School
Welcome to Hever School! We pride ourselves on being a small, friendly school set in a beautiful village that offers its children outstanding learning opportunities. We believe that a true measure of a school is not only what a child has achieved by the end of Year 6 but what they have done when they are eighty - we want to have a life-long influence on every child and instil a curiosity and a love of learning. Ours is a passionate, engaging and caring environment that will challenge your child to fulfil their potential.
The pastoral care and welfare of each child is of paramount importance. Our excellent care and support, which is an important part of the curriculum, ensures that every child is nurtured and valued. Should a child require any additional support, our excellent Special Educational Needs provision ensures that they receive prompt and appropriate provision within the classroom or with one to one support from our highly trained teaching assistants. We are an inclusive school, committed to providing equal opportunities for everyone regardless of gender, race, religion, belief or ability.
We seek to inspire learning and enjoyment in original and imaginative ways. We have innovative, award-winning teachers who foster intellectual debate, critical thinking and independence in our wonderful student body. Our creative curriculum encourages excitement in, and engages with, all the requirements of the National Curriculum. It has been designed to inspire and motivate pupils and to make learning purposeful. Our curriculum is enhanced through the many visitors to school from different areas of expertise and themed weeks. There are also many opportunities to take part in extra-curricular activities, team events and regular educational trips.
Teaching staff, volunteers and older students offer a wide variety of clubs which include a number of sports, musical activities and seasonal pursuits, such as gardening and cooking. We are proud of our broad and enriching extra-curricular programme and encourage all students to fully participate. Our school teams play in the local leagues and Kent Games championships, as well as taking part in inter-school events.
Hever Primary School is a Church of England School and Christianity is at the heart of everything we do. Our daily whole school worship reinforces and promotes our core values of Love, Respect and Wisdom. Children are encouraged to actively participate in all the Church services they attend. We have strong links with St Peter’s Church and regularly visit for worship and praise and to develop the children's Christian understanding and their spiritual beliefs.
We hope this will give you an insight into life at Hever Primary School, but we would encourage you to visit us to see what we have to offer and how we can support your child to flourish and grow. High academic expectations and pastoral care, together with a strong Christian ethos, ensure that every child flourishes and is challenged to reach his or her full potential.
We are a busy, happy, unique community; do come and visit us. You will be very welcome!
If you would like to discuss anything with our Headteacher or visit the school, please contact the school office on 01732 862304 or email us at office@hever.kent.sch.uk.

Admissions Arrangements including Appeals
Admission to Primary School including Appeals
We aim to make the transition to primary school as smooth as possible for both parents and children. With this in mind, we would encourage all prospective parents to visit the school in advance. Please email the school office to make an appointment. Applications for Hever Primary School will need to be made online directly to your local authority.
As we are a Church of England Voluntary Aided school we also require an additional clerical information form to be completed for faith-based applications which can be obtained from the school office, or by clicking on the form Clerical Reference Form below. This form should be returned directly to Hever Primary School.
If your child is due to start Primary school in September 2026 you can appeal if you are refused a place at one of your preferred schools on National Offer Day (Thursday, 16 April 2026). You needed to submit your appeal before Monday 18 May 2026 for it to be considered by Friday 20 July 2026. Any appeals received after this time will be heard within 40 school days from the deadline, or where reasonably possible in line with updated guidance from the Department for Education. For late applications, appeals should be heard within 40 school days from the deadline for lodging appeals where possible, or within 30 school days of the appeal being lodged where reasonably possible in line with updated guidance from the Department for Education.

Meet the Governors
Welcome to our Governors’ Section
Building the confidence and resilience to flourish
Education is the greatest opportunity young people have to achieve lifelong success and, together with our team of enthusiastic and dedicated staff, we are committed to ensuring that your children get the best possible education at Hever Primary School and succeed in achieving to the very best of their abilities and beyond.
The role of a school governor is far reaching with a wide range of possibilities. Governors help to form the school’s strategic aims, policies and targets and support the school’s drive for improvement. They act as ‘critical friends’ to the school through monitoring and evaluating progress and ensuring compliance with statutory responsibilities.
Full Governing Body meetings are held each term and Governors usually serve a term of four years on the Governing Body.
Below you will find details of the Governing Body, our vision and values for the school, how the Governing Body is structured, our roles and responsibilities together with information regarding our regular meetings.
The governors are currently collecting data on the diversity of the board, including data on age, gender and ethnicity. They will use that data to inform their recruitment and training needs and ensure there is always a diverse range of perspectives around the table to support robust decision making.
Due to our relatively small governing board, we will not publish this diversity data online as individual governors could be identified and we have a legal obligation to protect their personal data
If you would like to contact the Governing Body, please address your letter to the Chair of Governors, c/o Hever Primary School, Hever, Kent, TN8 7NH

pageCache.pageTitle: Hever C of E Primary School - Sports Premium
pageCache.text:
Sports Premium
About the PE and sport Premium Funding
Schools have a central role to play in supporting all children and young people to live healthy active lives. This is particularly true of primary school where the foundations of positive and enjoyable participation in regular physical activity should be established. Crucial to achieving this is ensuring that pupils have access to at least 30 minutes of physical activity during the school day, alongside high-quality PE provision taught by confident and knowledgeable teachers and opportunities to experience and participate in a wide range of sports and physical activities. PE and sport premium grant funding should be used by schools towards these aims.
We believe that the Sport Premium funding should support three key areas: physical education, healthy & active lifestyles and participation in competitions and local initiatives in the community. Our rationale at Hever Primary School is that the funding should be used in a fully inclusive manner, to benefit all pupils, not just those who excel in sports. We believe in nurturing talent and in giving opportunities to try a range of sports.

Wellbeing and Spirituality
Welcome to our Wellbeing and Spirituality page.
At Hever Primary School we are pleased to be able to work with the Kent Emotional Wellbeing Trust (KEWT)
Our KEWT Emotional Wellbeing Practitioner is Lucy Bishop. We have been extremely lucky to have the KEWT supporting our children with 1:1 and small group support, as well as offering advice and strategies for parents to support their child. They have even delivered friendship workshops and transition support over the past two years they have been working with us.
PARENT WORKSHOPS Please find the workshops that are on offer from the Kent Emotional Wellbeing Team during term 4. The remaining workshops are, 'Autism and Sleep' on the 9th March 12.30pm-3.30pm and 'Understanding Neurodiversity' on the 24th March from 10.30am until 12.30pm. However, if you have missed a workshop you felt would have been useful, keep checking back to this page, as workshops often get repeated.
OSI (ONLINE SUPPORT AND INTERVENTION FOR CHILD ANXIETY) OSI can empower parents to support their children with a range of anxieties including bedtime fears, school and social worries. Parent work through weekly online modules that contain videos, quizzes and interactive worksheets. Parents are also supported by a weekly telephone/video call with a practitioner and all can be carried out at a convenient time for you. Please read the poster for further information.
If you have any questions about the Emotional Wellbeing Team, please email Mrs Seymour (SENDCo) or the school office for more information.
At Hever, we believe that nurturing the spiritual development of every child is central to our Christian vision. Spirituality supports pupils in exploring meaning, purpose, and their relationship with God, themselves, others, and the world.
This document reflects our commitment to the Church of England Vision for Education and the statutory requirement for pupils’ spiritual, moral, social, and cultural (SMSC) development. We aim to create a school environment where all children, regardless of faith background, can flourish spiritually.
‘Jesus offers us a broader, deeper, social, moral, cultural, relational, spiritual life that is far beyond whether we are simply alive or not.’
Church of England, Our Hope for a Flourishing Schools System.
Our interpretation of Spirituality
Spirituality is widely recognised as difficult to define, as it means different things to different people. At Hever, our understanding of spirituality reflects a shared collection of thoughts, experiences and values from across our school community.
Spirituality at Hever School is about connection — to ourselves, to others, to the natural world, and to something greater than ourselves. It is the essence of living, inviting us to pause, notice, reflect, respond to and celebrate both the ordinary and extraordinary moments of life. Spirituality is deeply personal, unique to each individual, yet it can also be shared, flourishing in relationships, community, and a sense of belonging.
It involves self-reflection, empathy, and understanding — of our own experiences and those of others — and supports our well-being, peace, and sense of purpose. Spirituality can be found in the little things, like the wonder of the first snowdrop of spring, as well as in profound moments of connection, joy, or shared emotion. It encourages us to celebrate what brings us joy, nurtures our individuality, and helps us shine in the world.
Spirituality also recognises the presence of something beyond ourselves, whether experienced through faith, awe, creativity, or a sense of interconnectedness. It enables us to feel part of something larger than our individual selves, to understand our place in the wider world, and to engage with life with awareness, gratitude, and wonder.
At its heart, spirituality is about flourishing — as individuals and as a community — through awareness, connection, reflection, and the courage to explore the depths of our own experiences and those of the world around us. It permeates all aspects of life, supporting growth, resilience, empathy, and the capacity to live fully and meaningfully.

pageCache.pageTitle: Hever C of E Primary School - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Our curriculum is ambitious for all pupils, ensuring all our children experience the challenge and enjoyment of learning within a supportive community that fosters the courage to try and the determination to persevere. We have high expectations for all our children and strive to deliver a broad and balanced education enabling every child to achieve and succeed.
We use published schemes to provide a clear and progressive framework to deliver the National Curriculum, enabling children to build rich and deep subject knowledge and to develop their skills in a highly organised and structured way. Topics and schemes are adapted to be relevant to the experience of our children where possible and delivered in a way that excites, promotes and sustains children’s interest. This includes using quality resources and offering opportunities for children to learn in and out of the classroom.
We aim to build independent learners who have the skills and desire to communicate and collaborate effectively, in their learning and their play. We aim to build independent thinkers who develop strong links between different aspects of their learning and have the flexibility and adaptability to apply these in new and creative ways. We aim to build independent young people who are responsible and respectful, who are ready for the challenges and successes of their secondary education and to play their part in our diverse society beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: Hever C of E Primary School - Collective Worship
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
Worship and Christian Life at the School
There is a daily act of worship, which is a highly valued part of each school day. Grace is said before meals and a prayer is shared at the end of the school day.
Assemblies are led by the Head Teacher, staff, the pupils or clergy. It is an opportunity for the pupils to learn about God as Father, Son and Holy Spirit and to understand the teachings of the Bible. Each week we focus on a different Christian value. In our acts of Worship, Bible teachings are related to the school’s values and to the daily lives of the pupils.
To help the children gain a greater understanding of the Hever School values, each term we have a focus on one during our acts of worship. They are reflected on in the following order:
Term 3 - Perseverance
Term 6 - Chance to revisit all
A lively, creative approach includes readings, drama, prayers and music. We use a variety of well-known hymns and modern worship songs, and the pupils actively participate and enjoy worship. It is also a time for quiet prayer and reflection focusing on our school values.
We have strong links with St Peter’s Church and the local community in Hever and Edenbridge. The main church services each year are: Harvest, Remembrance, Christingle, KS2 Carol Service, Easter and Year 6 Leavers' Service.
All of the collective worship activities that the pupils take part in help to support and deepen the school community's understanding of what we stand for as a Church school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Hever C of E Primary School - Ofsted Report
pageCache.text:
Ofsted Report
Extracts from our Ofsted report:
The school is highly ambitious for pupils’ academic achievement and their character development. Pupils learn how to be emotionally resilient, so they can challenge themselves to learn more deeply and confidently.
Right from entering Reception, pupils learn the school’s clear behaviour expectations. These are consistently reinforced through well understood routines. Relationships between adults and pupils are full of warmth and mutual respect. Adults are consistent role models in kindness and working together as a team.
Adults and pupils alike are inspired by the school’s ambitious vision. Staff are proud to be part of this team. The curriculum is broad and ambitious. It sets out coherently the most important areas that pupils must understand and remember.
Ofsted Inspection Report October 2024
